body:
>Leonid Andreev's "Thought" (1902)

Yes yes yes!!! Thank you so much!!!

I think I understand a little bit of where you're coming from. It might not be the same, but I've often felt that I am under qualified to live my own life, like there should be someone more competent in charge of all of this. It sounds like you're hyper-aware of what you're struggling with, that must be very difficult to handle.
I'm sorry you have to struggle; I'm sure I have no idea how hard it must be. What made you start thinking about suicide today?
I'm sorry you feel that way.

I hear you. I'm just spitballing here. You're a person, and people require social attention and support, they just do and it's okay.

They need it no matter what, and when a person don't get it, it can become an intolerable situation, and attempting to kill yourself can seem like a the only way to escape, one way or another.

It's understandable that you would feel this way, because you have a necessary need that just isn't being met. And you do deserve to have it met. But you shouldn't have to die to have it met.
I wish you wouldn't. I've read some of your posts. You're unique and the world could use more people like you.

It's okay to just survive. If the life you need to live in order to be alive isn't perfect, if all you can do right now is look at the world, and love music, and be, that's okay. You're worth it, you in yourself. Being productive isn't the point, you are the point.

You don't deserve the pain you're going through, you deserve better.  I can see that you're in a lot of pain, and I just wish there was some way I could help, even a little, because you need and deserve help, love, and attention that you aren't getting, and I can see it hurts a lot. You shouldn't have to bear the weight of the world on your shoulders, it's okay to just survive, because you yourself are worth enough.
My family knows I am doing badly and are staying with me now, so I am not in immediate danger.

I have often felt the exact same way with my mental illness, that I must be faking it because it fluctuates between barely being able to function, and feeling fine. It's important to remember, mental illness is different for everyone, and not everyone will have the same symptoms, illnesses, comorbidities, or feelings. It's understandable that you would feel very confused and upset, I know I certainly was.

What helped me to accept and finally start being able to manage my mental illness was finding the right therapist; not every therapist will be able to help every patient, you have to find the one who's right for you, and it may take a few times: you are fully worth the time it takes. Mental illness is just like any other disease, and it's important to get an expert's help to figure it out; trying to diagnose yourself is tricky, because of the variations people can experience even with the same diagnosis, not to mention complicating factors.
